title: What If One Second Felt Like a Year?

shots.scene: kitchen wide, warm afternoon: Grandpa dancing by the record player, Leo at the table, slow push

shots.line: Your grandpa is dancing in the kitchen, the way he always does.
shots.scene: medium: Grandpa dances, tapping the counter, music notes

shots.line: Then his hand slips off the counter.
shots.scene: insert: Grandpa's hand slides off the counter edge
medium: Grandpa's knees buckle, Leo turns
bigFace Leo shocked
TIME FREEZE: the kitchen stops, blue tint, everything hangs

shots.line: His glasses hang in the air.
shots.scene: insert: Grandpa's glasses floating in the air

shots.line: A spoon floats above the floor.
shots.scene: insert: a spoon hanging above the floor tiles

shots.line: The music holds one long note.
shots.scene: record player: one long flat sound wave
wide frozen kitchen, slow pull back
bigFace Leo frozen, eyes fixed

shots.line: You’re standing inside a single second.
shots.scene: Leo stands tiny on a giant frozen clock face

shots.line: And you’re about to live a whole year in it.
shots.scene: calendar pages flip DAY 1 to 365; 1 SECOND = 1 YEAR

shots.line: Three weeks earlier, it happened for the very first time.
shots.scene: dip: bedroom morning, label THREE WEEKS EARLIER

shots.line: Your name is Leo. You’re fifteen.
shots.scene: Leo medium, labels LEO and AGE 15

shots.line: A year holds about thirty-one and a half million seconds.
shots.scene: counter races to 31,500,000 SECONDS

shots.line: Most people feel each one as... just a second.
shots.scene: line figures, each second ticks past as just 1 s
bigFace Leo smirk

shots.line: Hold your breath, and one second stretches into a full year.
shots.scene: Leo inhales, blue freeze spreads; 1 SECOND = 1 YEAR

shots.line: A year to think. To remember. To plan.
shots.scene: THINK, REMEMBER, PLAN icons pop on the words
bigLine THE RULE
line figure: brain glowing gold, thoughts sparking
body locked grey with a padlock
insert: frozen finger, lock icon
bigFace Leo, eyes locked in place

shots.line: You can think anything... but you can’t do anything.
shots.scene: split: THINK yes, DO no
Leo breathes out, colour returns

shots.line: So what if one second felt like a year?
shots.scene: TITLE CARD: WHAT IF ONE SECOND FELT LIKE A YEAR?

shots.line: The first time is a maths test.
shots.scene: classroom wide: maths test, students writing, clock
insert: test paper, QUESTION 7, scary equation

shots.line: You hold your breath... and you get a whole year with it.
shots.scene: bigFace Leo holds breath, freeze flash
frozen classroom; thought bubble: equation solved

shots.line: Then you solve it three more ways.
shots.scene: bubble: three more methods, ticks

shots.line: Then you get bored and invent a board game in your head.
shots.scene: bubble: a board game builds itself in Leo's head
unfreeze, colour returns
insert: wall clock, second hand barely moved

shots.line: Leo, you finished in four minutes?
shots.scene: bigFace teacher amazed, talking
Leo smirks, talking: plenty of time
PLUS badge; chess club, Leo vs the champion

shots.line: Every move gets a year of thought.
shots.scene: top-down chess board, a piece glows; 1 YEAR PER MOVE

shots.line: You beat the school champion in eleven moves.
shots.scene: checkmate; champion facepalms; 11 MOVES

shots.line: Your best friend Jake stares at you.
shots.scene: Jake stares at Leo, shocked
bigFace Jake talking
Leo shrugs, talking

shots.line: Mate. That was a very scary second.
shots.scene: Jake leans back nervously, talking
football pitch at golden hour: Leo in goal, striker at the spot

shots.line: A hard penalty reaches the goal in about half a second.
shots.scene: diagram: spot to goal 11 m, ball arrives in 0.5 s

shots.line: You hold your breath as the ball leaves the boot.
shots.scene: striker kicks; the ball leaves the boot; freeze
frozen ball macro, spin arrows; SPIN
goal diagram: ANGLE, then a gold line to the TOP CORNER
bigFace Leo frozen in his gloves

shots.line: You can’t dive any faster than any other keeper.
shots.scene: two keepers' dive bars: SAME SPEED

shots.line: You just dive the right way... first time.
shots.scene: Leo dives toward the right corner
insert: glove fingertips tip the ball
ball deflects wide; Jake celebrates
MINUS badge; an eye-shaped frame around one frozen picture

shots.line: So for a whole year, you stare at one frozen picture.
shots.scene: the frozen picture, DAY counter crawling
frozen picture: a sunset over the city
frozen picture: Jake mid-sneeze, droplets hanging

shots.line: For three hundred and sixty-five days.
shots.scene: same sneeze; DAY 365 counter

shots.line: Your heart beats roughly once a second.
shots.scene: heartbeat line, one beat per second

shots.line: So inside the year, you hear one heartbeat.
shots.scene: one beat stretched across a whole year timeline
a single glowing heart pulse

shots.line: Like a door closing very, very slowly.
shots.scene: a door closing very slowly in the dark

shots.line: But where it gets really crazy... is a storm.
shots.scene: night storm over the city, rain

shots.line: A lightning flash is over in less than a second.
shots.scene: lightning flashes; label UNDER 1 SECOND

shots.line: You get to watch it crawl across the sky... for months.
shots.scene: TIME FREEZE: lightning grows branch by branch, Leo at the window; FOR MONTHS
bigFace Leo sad in the dark

shots.line: Every time you use it, you live another year.
shots.scene: years stack up: +1 YEAR, +1 YEAR

speech bubbles fade away
a hand reaches into nothing

shots.line: Just your thoughts and one frozen picture.
shots.scene: Leo with one frozen picture floating in front of him
Leo medium; AGE 15

shots.line: But you’ve used it forty times.
shots.scene: 40 tally marks

shots.line: Which means... you’ve lived forty years nobody saw.
shots.scene: Leo's shadow on the wall is an old man; 40 YEARS NOBODY SAW

shots.line: Scientists know long isolation is hard on the human brain.
shots.scene: brain inside an isolation box

shots.line: People kept alone for long stretches often report anxiety, confusion, even seeing things that aren’t there.
shots.scene: ANXIETY, CONFUSION, SEEING THINGS appear on the words
Leo in his room at night; shapes creep in the shadows
hallway: Jake looks at tired Leo

shots.line: Dude. You sigh like my dad.
shots.scene: bigFace Jake talking
a question mark grows huge

shots.line: What if one day... you can’t make yourself breathe out?
shots.scene: frozen forever: breath held, clock never restarts
kitchen evening: Leo and Grandpa at the table
bigFace Grandpa, kind eyes behind glasses

shots.line: He doesn’t laugh. He just nods.
shots.scene: two-shot: Grandpa nods slowly

shots.line: A whole year alone? Then don’t go in empty-handed.
shots.scene: bigFace Grandpa talking
Grandpa holds up a vinyl record, talking

shots.line: The same old disco record he dances to every Sunday, tapping the counter.
shots.scene: Grandpa dancing, tapping the counter, record spinning

shots.line: About a hundred beats a minute.
shots.scene: metronome swinging: 100 BEATS / MIN

shots.line: You hum it inside every frozen year, so the silence isn’t silent.

shots.line: And whenever you worry, he says the same thing.
shots.scene: Grandpa's hand on Leo's shoulder, talking

shots.line: A second is plenty, Leo... if you use it.

shots.line: Can you even remember the steps?

shots.scene: the class repeats; counter x1000

shots.line: But in here, nothing gets worse.

endless frozen space

shots.line: A second is plenty. And for the first time in forty years... you’re not alone.
shots.scene: two-shot in warm light

shots.line: People often say time slowed down during a scare.
shots.scene: line figure scared, clock slowing?

shots.line: In 2007, neuroscientist David Eagleman tested it.
shots.scene: 2007: DAVID EAGLEMAN

shots.line: Volunteers fell about thirty meters into a net while watching a display flash numbers too fast to read.
shots.scene: 30 m drop into a net, wrist display flashing numbers

shots.line: If time really slowed, they could read them.
shots.scene: the display: numbers too fast to read
a red X

shots.line: Their brains just recorded more. Frightening moments get stored in richer detail, so they feel longer afterward.
shots.scene: memory frames pile up densely

shots.line: And the CPR part? That’s real.

shots.line: If someone collapses and isn’t breathing normally, call emergency services and push hard and fast in the center of the chest.
